blockers.summary: A short canonical label exposed an unresolved scoring-policy ambiguity.
A candidate label could also be a correct answer surface form for another item.
Some relations admitted multiple directors, countries, or citizenships.
Some person occupation questions did not have one determinate answer.
Some English labels identified multiple plausible entities.
Some accepted aliases were unsafe abbreviations or pseudonym-like surfaces.
Some country and administrative answers used inconsistent granularity or codes.
Some facts were ambiguous between historical and current values.
